payload.content: Yes. For most healthy adults it is safe to take ibuprofen and acetaminophen (paracetamol) together or to alternate them, because they work in different ways and do not interact with each other. Keep each within its own label limit: generally no more than 3,000–4,000 mg of acetaminophen per day, and no more than 1,200 mg of over-the-counter ibuprofen per day unless a doctor says otherwise. People with kidney disease, stomach ulcers, liver disease, heart problems, or who are pregnant should check with a doctor or pharmacist first.
